_note: Real radiation numbers the game is built on. Owner: role 06. Plain words: 1 mSv (millisievert) is a unit of how much radiation the body got. On Earth a person gets about 2-3 mSv in a WHOLE YEAR from nature. On the ISS an astronaut gets about 0.5 mSv EVERY DAY, so in ~5 days as much as on Earth in a year.
_status: Checked 2026-11-15 against NASA documents (see sources): ISS crews get about 0.5 mSv per day (NASA LSAH newsletter 2023), 80-160 mSv in a 6-month stay depending on solar activity (NASA-STD-3001 radiation technical brief), career limit 600 mSv (NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 Rev B). NOT checked against the RadLab time series: the RadLab site (visualization.osdr.nasa.gov/radlab/) answered HTTP 500 on that day, so the numbers are NASA's published typical values, not a RadLab query.
dailyDose_note: Typical ISS dose equivalent per day. NASA: ISS crew receive about 80-160 mSv in a 6-month stay = about 0.44-0.88 mSv per day; we use 0.5.
careerLimit_note: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 (2022): career limit of 600 mSv for every astronaut. In the game Dose = % of this limit.
stormNote: During a solar particle event the dose rate rises for hours to days. Inside the thick-walled parts of the ISS it rises only a little; on the open Moon surface it can be many times higher. That is why the game has a shelter.
